mcat_description.short: Guard huts are compact prefabricated structures used to shelter security personnel at entry and exit points of residential, commercial, and industrial premises. They are sold as ready-to-install or semi-knocked-down units in steel, FRP, PUF-panel, or PVC construction.
mcat_description.long: Guard huts — also widely called security cabins, guard rooms, or watchman rooms — are factory-built portable structures designed to provide a functional workspace for on-duty security guards at gates, checkpoints, and access control points. They are manufactured using a mild steel or GI frame with wall panels of FRP, PUF sandwich panels, EPS, cement fibre board (CFB), or GI sheet, and are available in standard footprints ranging from 4×4 ft to 8×8 ft with custom sizes on request. Key features include weather resistance, thermal insulation, pre-fitted electrical conduits, sliding windows, and lockable doors, making them suitable for year-round outdoor deployment without a permanent foundation. The Indian market is served by a large base of prefab manufacturers concentrated in NCR (Faridabad, Noida, Gurgaon), Ahmedabad, Pune, and Chennai, with both readymade and made-to-order supply models.

market_context: Guard huts in the Indian B2B market are predominantly sold as prefabricated portable security cabins, with mild steel (MS) and FRP being the two dominant material types; PUF-insulated panel cabins are a growing premium sub-segment favoured for all-weather comfort. Standard commercial sizes are 4×4 ft, 4×6 ft, 6×6 ft, 6×8 ft, and 8×8 ft, with custom dimensions available from most manufacturers. The Indian manufacturing base is concentrated in NCR (Faridabad, Noida, Gurgaon), Ahmedabad, and Pune, with pan-India delivery. Buyers include housing societies, industrial facilities, real estate developers, and security agencies. The product is sold both as a readymade/pre-assembled unit and as a semi-knocked-down (SKD) kit for on-site assembly. No mandatory BIS or IS standard governs guard huts specifically; quality is assessed by material grade, insulation type, and structural durability. The buyer vocabulary strongly favours 'guard room' and 'security cabin' over 'guard hut' (confirmed by Google keyword data: 'guard room' = 237 impressions vs 'guard huts' = lower internal volume). Container-based guard rooms are an emerging variant for buyers needing larger or more permanent structures. The Hindi trade term 'चौकी घर' (chowki ghar) is used in buyer search queries (22 Google impressions at position 2).
